 Bill Shannon Sun, November 15, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. FAYETTE COUNTY, Pa. (WTAJ) -- A Uniontown City Council member was charged with taking nearly $7,000 from SNAP and LIHEAP by failing to report wages from his job at Senior LIFE.
 Trace Thomas, 34, was charged with a third-degree felony for allegedly making false statements to collect benefits, the Office of State Inspector General said. Trace allegedly collected $6,705 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) benefits by failing to report $166,637.61 in wages from his job between Nov. 9, 2023, and Sept. 30, 2025.
 Thomas repeatedly told the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services that he had no income, leading to him collecting $5,705 in SNAP benefits and $1,000 in LIHEAP benefits over nearly two years.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Public assistance programs exist so Pennsylvanians can bridge the gap and make ends meet," said Fayette County District Attorney Michael Aubele. "Mr. Thomas abused this system, and together with OSIG, we were able to stop this abuse from continuing and protect the integrity of these important programs."
 Thomas took office on the Uniontown City Council in January 2024 and, according to Uniontown City's website, oversees the city's Streets and Improvements department.
 "This case shows our commitment to rooting out public benefits fraud wherever we find it," said State Inspector General Michelle A. Henry. "Trace Thomas holds a position of public trust as a member of Uniontown City Council, yet he is charged with knowingly misleading the Commonwealth again and again to collect benefits meant for Pennsylvanians in need. No one is above the law. I am grateful to the Fayette County District Attorney's Office for their work with this investigation."
 In 2025 alone, after investigating nearly 20,000 applications, the Shapiro Administration saved taxpayers over $61 million, the Office added.
